To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heating effect of cooking on P. vulgaris significantly (P< 0.05) increases the phytochemical and proximate contents of the plant.
cooking significantly reduced crude fibre, crude fat, tannins, alkaloids and sponins.
the heating of kidney bean increased the protein and carbohydrate contents, but reduced the crude fat, tannins, glycosides, alkaloids and saphonins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of heating on phytochemical and proximate contents of cooked aqueous extract of Phaseolus vulgarus.
the effects of heat treatment on the phytoconstituents and proximate contents of P. vulgaris.
phytochemicals of Phaseolus vulgar.

cooking significantly increased the levels of phytochemical constituents in cooked P. vulgairs (Kidney Beans) and also significantly increased the levels and concentrations of the proximate contents of cooked P. vulgariss (Kidney Beans).
the heating effect on phytochemical and proximate content of kidney bean could improve its nutritional value.
cooking P. vulgaris significantly reduced the crude fibre content, crude protein, crude ash, crude fat and saponins, while it increased the carbohydrate and protein contents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cooking significantly improved the nutritional quality of P. vulgaris.
the heating effect of P. vulgaris increased the level of phytochemical contents in CKB and also increased the level of nutrients in CKB.
the phytochemical constituents in P. vulgaris are more abundant in the raw state than in the cooked state.
